nodes.name: Coprecipitation of PBAs
nodes.procedure: Five metal cations (MnII, CoII, NiII, CuII, and ZnII) from metal nitrates are selected as metal sources to fabricate a series of binary, ternary, quaternary, and HE PBAs using water as solvent by a simple room temperature coprecipitation method (detailed steps in Supporting Information). The amount of K₃[Fe(CN)₆] is fixed at 2 mmol, and the total moles of added other metal salts remain unchanged at 2 mmol. Different molar ratios are used: 1:3 for certain ternary PBAs (Cu/Ni, Ni/Co, etc.), 3:1 for others (Ni/Co, Cu/Ni, etc.), 2:1:1 for quaternary, and 1:1:1:1:1 for HE-PBA.
nodes.source_text: Five metal cations—MnII, CoII, NiII, CuII, and ZnII—from metal nitrates... The detailed steps of the synthetic process can be found in the Supporting Information.

nodes.name: Pyrolysis to metal oxides
nodes.procedure: A series of metal oxides including NiFe-oxide, CoFe-oxide, CoNiFe-oxide, NiCuFe-oxide, NiZnFe-oxide, CuZnFe-oxide, CoMnFe-oxide, and CoNiCuMnZnFe-oxide, were fabricated by the pyrolysis at 500°C in air for 2 h of NiFe-PBA, CoFe-PBA, CoNiFe-PBA, NiCuFe-PBA, NiZnFe-PBA, CuZnFe-PBA, CoMnFe-PBA, and HE-PBA, respectively.

nodes.name: Melt-diffusion sulfur loading
nodes.procedure: Through melt-diffusion approach at 130°C, sulfur molecules were well introduced into the pores of NiFe-PBA, NiCuFe-PBA, CoNiCuFe-PBA, and HE-PBA, labeled as NiFe-PBA-S, NiCuFe-PBA-S, CoNiCuFe-PBA-S, and HE-PBA-S.

nodes.characterization_summary: Binary PBAs NiFe-PBA (≈310 nm), CoFe-PBA (≈300 nm), CuFe-PBA (≈120 nm) exhibit regular cubic shape; MnFe-PBA shows uniform hollow sphere shape ≈1 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For binary PBAs, NiFe-PBA, CoFe-PBA, and CuFe-PBA exhibit regular cubic shape with particle sizes of ≈310, ≈300, and ≈120 nm, respectively (Figure 2a1-a3). Distinctly, MnFe-PBA shows a uniform hollow sphere shape with rough surface, and the particle size is about 1 μm (Figures 2a4 and S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images confirm morphologies and particle sizes of PBAs; HAADF-STEM elemental mapping demonstrates homogeneous distribution of Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn in HE-PBA face-centered cubic framework.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphologies were characterized through scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Figure 2) ... The high-angle annular dark field scanning TEM (HAADFSTEM) images and corresponding element mapping analysis demonstrate the homogeneous distribution of Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn in PBA face-centered cubic framework.

nodes.characterization_summary: All PBAs exhibit characteristic diffraction peaks of PBA with no superfluous peaks; (200) peaks shift from 17.3° for NiFe-PBA to 17.6° for HE-PBA indicating lattice shrinking.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The PXRD patterns of all PBAs exhibit a set of characteristic diffraction peaks of PBA, and no superfluous peaks for other phases are observed ... the (200) peaks of PBA are at 17.3°, 17.7°, 17.5°, 17.6°, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Composition of Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Mn and Zn measured confirming successful formation of PBAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The composition of Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Mn and Zn were mensurate by inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES), as shown in Table S1, demonstrating the successful formation of this series of PBAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES at Fe K-edge similar to Fe2O3, Co/Ni/Cu/Mn/Zn K-edges similar to their oxides (+2 state); EXAFS shows Fe-C, Co-N, Ni-N, Cu-N, Mn-N, Zn-N bonds confirming successful metal incorporation into PBA framework.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra at the Fe K-edge for NiFe-PBA, NiCuFe-PBA, CoNiCuFe-PBA, and HE-PBA ... XANES spectra for these PBAs at the Co, Ni, Cu, Mn and Zn K-edge are similar to those of CoO, NiO, CuO, MnO and ZnO ... The Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Mn and Zn K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectrum for these PBAs reveals obvious Fe-C, Co-N, Ni-N, Cu-N, Mn-N and Zn-N.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows obvious lattice fringes and SAED confirms good crystallinity of CoNiCuMnZnFe-oxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images exhibit obvious lattice fringe, which together with the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern confirm the good crystalline characteristics of CoNiCuMnZnFe-oxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: CoNiCuMnZnFe-oxide XPS shows Cu2+, Zn2+; Fe 2p, Co 2p, Ni 2p, Mn 2p indicate divalent/trivalent species; O 1s at 529.5 eV for metal-bound oxygen.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectra show that Cu and Zn cations mainly exist in the form of Cu²⁺ and Zn²⁺, respectively. The Fe 2p, Co 2p, Ni 2p, and Mn 2p spectra indicate that there are corresponding divalent and trivalent species. Notably, the O 1s spectra at 529.5 eV corresponds to oxygen atoms bound to metals.

nodes.characterization_summary: PBAs show -OH vibrations at 1607 cm⁻¹ and 3403 cm⁻¹, C≡N stretching at 2000-2200 cm⁻¹; oxides show disappearance of CN peaks after pyrolysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The weak peak at 1607 cm⁻¹ and the broad peak at 3403 cm⁻¹ in PBAs originate from the -OH bending vibration and stretching vibration of H₂O, respectively ... After oxidation of the PBA precursors at 500°C, the characteristic peaks of CN disappear.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping confirms homogeneous distribution of all metals in PBAs including HE-PBA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM images and corresponding elemental mapping analysis of binary PBAs (a1-a4), ternary PBAs (b1-b7), quaternary PBAs (c1-c4), and HE-PBA (d1 and d2).
